//: Firestore index configuration — the FIRST deliberate index management in this repo.
Before this file, every index in staging and production was either created
automatically by Firestore (single-field, COLLECTION scope) or clicked into a
console by hand. Neither is reproducible, and P2 introduces the first queries
that genuinely need an index that is NOT automatic.
WHY THESE TWO, AND ONLY THESE TWO
P2 moves devices from a root collection to users/{uid}/devices/{deviceId}. Two
queries then have to span parents, and a COLLECTION_GROUP query is not covered
by the automatic COLLECTION-scope single-field indexes:
deviceId  — the steal check on login (design section 4.1): which OTHER account
currently holds a session on this device?
lastSeen  — the abandoned-session sweep (design section 9), which needs every
device row older than the TTL regardless of account.
An earlier draft listed four. The field audit (design section 3.1) removed the
stations[] and lines[] arrays from the device row, and with them the only two
array-contains-any collection-group queries. That matters beyond tidiness: the
push-audience path is the one that fires during a disruption incident, and it
now touches no collection group at all.
A MISSING COLLECTION-GROUP INDEX FAILS THE QUERY OUTRIGHT. It does not degrade,
it does not get slower — it throws FAILED_PRECONDITION. So both must exist and
be verified BEFORE the code that depends on them goes live. Use:
node src/scripts/ensure_device_indexes.cjs --key=<sa>   # creates, idempotent
node src/scripts/check_device_indexes.cjs  --key=<sa>   # read-only proof
These are SINGLE-FIELD indexes with COLLECTION_GROUP scope, so they belong in
fieldOverrides rather than in `indexes` — `indexes` is for composite indexes,
and putting a single-field entry there is a common and silent mistake: the
deploy succeeds and the query still fails.
